column2: A slain person lies in the field with an unknown killer; the death-investigation context supports slain for traumatias here.
Elders and judges measure the distances to surrounding cities, preserving both offices and the location of the body.
The nearest city's elders provide a heifer never worked or yoked; both animal conditions remain.
The rough ravine is untilled and unsown, and the selected action cuts the heifer's sinews rather than substituting neck-breaking.
Levitical priests stand and bless in the Lord's name, with dispute and injury adjudicated by their word.
column3: The range of haphe in the paired legal categories remains open, as at 17:8.

column2: All nearby-city elders wash over the head of the sinew-cut heifer in the ravine; the selected head detail remains.
They deny both bloodshed by their hands and knowledge by their eyes, retaining the paired testimony.
Direct prayer uses Thy and Thou, recalls Egyptian redemption and seeks release from innocent-blood guilt; the final atonement statement returns to third-person narration.
Removal of innocent-blood guilt depends on doing good and pleasing before the Lord; guilt makes the legal force of the blood expression explicit.
War, divine delivery and taking spoil introduce the captive-marriage case.
The woman's appearance, the man's desire and taking her as wife remain, without adding reciprocal consent to the described captivity.
The selected second-person actions bring her home, shave her head and pare her nails; agency is not shifted to the woman.
Removing captivity garments and a month of mourning both parents precede marital cohabitation; the sequence and waiting period remain.
If unwanted, she goes free and cannot be sold for silver or treated with contempt because she has been humbled.
column3: The exact force of atheteo in the treatment prohibition needs further lexical review; contempt is provisional.

column2: Two wives, loved and hated, both bear children, and the firstborn belongs to the hated wife; the source's relational labels remain.
Distribution of possessions cannot promote the loved wife's son by overlooking the actual firstborn.
The hated wife's firstborn receives double from all possessions because he begins the children and holds the birthright.
Disobedience continues despite both parents' voices and discipline, defining the rebellious-son case.
Both parents seize him and bring him to city elders and the gate, retaining both agents and locations.
The parents allege disobedience, rebelliousness, failure to hear, carousing and drunkenness; all components remain.
City men stone him to death, remove the evil person, and leave the others hearing and fearing; the violent sentence is explicit.
A capital offense, death and subsequent hanging on wood appear in that order, without importing a different execution method.
Same-day burial prevents overnight display and land defilement; everyone hanging on wood is explicitly cursed by God in this selected text.
A brother's wandering calf or sheep must be returned and restored, preserving both actions and the no-disregard instruction.
If the owner is distant and unknown, the finder keeps the animals at home until they are sought and then returns them.
Donkey, garment and every other found lost object receive the same treatment; repeated so you shall do remains.
Fallen donkey or calf must be raised with the owner, retaining the assistance requirement and emphatic action.
The selected distinction between a man's equipment and a woman's robe remains; both actions receive the stated prohibition.
column3: Equipment for skeue is broader than clothing and needs contextual historical review before narrowing its scope.

column2: Nest location, young or eggs and the brooding mother are specified; mother and young may not be taken together.
The mother is emphatically released while young may be taken, with welfare and long days as stated purposes.
A roof parapet prevents fatal liability when someone falls, preserving the practical construction and consequence.
A different vineyard crop risks consecrating seed and produce together with the vineyard yield; selected consecrated is not changed to spoiled.
Calf and donkey must not plough together; selected calf remains rather than an unmarked adult-ox substitution.
Mixed wool and linen in one garment are prohibited, preserving the two named materials.
Twisted tassels belong on all four edges of outer garments, retaining construction, number and location.
Marriage, cohabitation and hatred introduce the accusation case.
Pretextual charges and an evil name accompany the allegation of missing virginity tokens; the allegation remains quoted rather than asserted as fact.
Both parents bring the tokens before elders at the gate, preserving the evidentiary action and participants.
The father reports giving his daughter in marriage and the husband's hatred, introducing his reply.
Propose and now he himself for and behold, he. Selected autos nyn supplies personal emphasis and now, not an unexpressed behold. The allegation, counterevidence and spreading of the garment remain.
The elders take and discipline the man after the presented defense; no specific unexpressed number of blows is added.
The fine is one hundred shekels to the father, with continuing marriage and a lifelong bar on dismissal; the selected monetary unit remains.
A true accusation with missing tokens introduces the alternative judgment, retaining both conditions.
The woman is brought to her father's doors and killed by city men, with the stated folly and harlotry reason retained without added moral commentary.
A man found with a married woman and the woman are both put to death; both parties are expressly repeated.
The betrothed virgin is encountered in a city, setting up the specified urban case.
Both are brought to the city gate for death, and the text gives distinct reasons concerning no cry and violation of a neighbour's wife; these remain the law's stated reasons.
The field case explicitly uses force and kills only the man, preserving the crucial exception.
Nothing is done to the woman because no capital sin is hers; comparison with a murderous attack is retained.
She cries out in the field and has no helper, preserving the explanation for her lack of liability.
The unbetrothed case also explicitly uses force in the selected Greek; it is not softened to consensual intercourse, and he is found out remains singular.
Fifty silver didrachmas, marriage and a lifelong bar on dismissal follow the violation; didrachmas is not harmonized to the earlier shekels.
Taking the father's wife and uncovering his covering are prohibited at the selected new-chapter opening.
The two bodily conditions bar entry into the assembly; the inherited anatomical explanation remains restrained and explicit.
Selected one born of a prostitute remains, without importing an additional tenth-generation clause into this unit.
Ammonite and Moabite exclusion includes tenth generation and forever, preserving both time expressions.
Lack of bread-and-water welcome and hiring Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia are the two reasons; no additional origin town is supplied.
The Lord refuses Balaam and turns plural curses into a blessing because of His love, retaining the number contrast.
Propose nor words to their advantage for nor seek their advantage: the selected speaking verb governs both peaceful and beneficial speech, without an expressed seek verb. The full duration remains.
An Edomite is a brother and Egypt was a place of sojourning, so neither people is to be abhorred; both stated reasons remain.
Their descendants enter the assembly in the third generation, preserving the specified threshold.
Encamping against enemies requires guarding against every evil thing, introducing camp purity rules.
Nocturnal discharge entails leaving and not entering the camp, retaining both movement clauses.
Evening washing and sunset precede re-entry; both temporal steps remain.
An outside place is designated for going out, preserving the camp distinction.
A peg on the belt is used for digging and covering excrement after squatting outside; the selected implement is not replaced with a modern tool.
The Lord's presence, rescue and delivery of enemies require a holy camp without indecency that would occasion His departure.
A slave who has joined the community from his master is not to be handed back, preserving the prohibition and direction of movement.
He chooses a pleasing residence among them and must not be afflicted; the repeated dwelling clauses remain.
Both prostitution prohibitions and both initiation-related prohibitions remain, preserving the fuller selected text.
column3: Telesphoros and teliskomenos require specialist history-of-religion and lexical review; inherited initiation-role descriptions remain provisional.

column2: A prostitute's hire and a dog's price are both excluded from the Lord's house for a vow; dog is not silently replaced with a speculative identification.
Interest on silver, food and anything lent to a brother is forbidden, retaining all three categories.
Foreign lending at interest is distinguished from the brother prohibition, with blessing in the inherited land as the stated purpose.
Propose sin in you for sin upon you to retain the selected en soi. A vow must not be delayed because the Lord emphatically requires it.
Propose no sin in you for no sin upon you, preserving the same selected construction in the contrasting case of not choosing to vow.
What leaves lips must be kept and done as the vowed gift spoken by the mouth, retaining the repeated speech imagery.
Hand-gathering ears is allowed but a sickle is barred in a neighbour's harvest; this grain case precedes the vineyard in the selected order.
Grapes may satisfy the eater but none go into a container, preserving the limit and final selected unit.
